title: Embedding quantization tuning and drift validation lab
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Runbook and experimental ticket for producing production-ready INT8/FP16 quantization profiles for embedding models, plus a cosine-similarity drift validation pipeline. This work covers: (1) an automated calibration harness that sweeps per-layer and per-channel scale strategies; (2) synthetic and production holdout datasets to validate cosine similarity retention; (3) a lightweight drift detection service that raises flags when median-topk cosine drops exceed thresholds; (4) rollout gating and rollback procedures for Dedicated and Private deployments. We will treat FP16 as the baseline reduced-precision target with INT8 as the optimized cost point; FP8 exploratory notes are captured separately but are not part of initial acceptance criteria.
acceptance_criteria: Calibration harness can generate and persist a config bundle (scale tables + quant strategy) for a given checkpoint and training seed

End-to-end validation run produces: (a) median cosine similarity >= 0.995 against FP32 baseline for production holdout; (b) 99th-percentile similarity drop <= 0.01 across corpus; (c) no downstream rerank regression > 0.5% in label-based micro-F1 for three representative tasks
Automated nightly drift job runs and emits metrics to the Console dashboard and Prometheus with alerts when rolling 7-day median-topk cosine decreases by >0.015
Can perform controlled canary rollout of quantized profile to Dedicated pool with automatic rollback on drift or error spike
Playbook documented in Confluence with troubleshooting steps and a runbook for manual recalibration
Unit and integration tests for calibration logic and similarity computations with >=90% coverage for the harness modules
steps: 1) Build calibration harness: support per-channel symmetric, per-layer asymmetric, and mixed scale policies. Implement sampling hooks to lock RNG for reproducibility.

2) Select holdout datasets: (a) small curated corpus (n=10k) reflecting search queries, (b) customer-privacy-safe production sample (n=50k) stratified by tenant and content length, (c) synthetic adversarial perturbations to validate corner cases.
3) Sweep quant params: grid over bit-width (INT8 variants), clip thresholds, outlier-capping strategy, and layer grouping heuristics. Persist scorecards for each run.
4) Validation: compute pairwise cosine similarity distributions vs FP32 baseline, per-bucket (length, domain). Produce summary percentiles and visualizations.
5) Drift detection: implement rolling window comparator that emits topk median cosine and exposes an anomaly time-series to Alertmanager.
6) Rollout gating: integrate with Console rollouts to allow canary_percent and automatic revert when alerts/triggers fire.
7) Documentation: Confluence design doc, ops playbook, and PR linking. Add samples to SDK docs showing how to request quant profiles via API.
8) Release: cut runtime-1.20 candidate with quant profile support and enable in staging Dedicated pools for soak testing. Monitor metrics for 72 hours.
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: subtle distribution shift leads to embedding drift undetected by global median metrics. Mitigation: add per-tenant and per-corpus buckets; require no regression for any critical customer test set before rollout.

Risk: calibration overfits to the small holdout and fails in tail workloads. Mitigation: use ensemble of calibration seeds and cross-validate across multiple corpora; prefer conservative scale factors when uncertainty is high.

Risk: performance regressions on throughput due to per-channel quant overhead. Mitigation: measure end-to-end P99 latency and throughput; provide an FPS/cost tradeoff dashboard and a configuration knob to toggle group-quant vs per-channel.
Risk: silent failures during Private rollout. Mitigation: include health-check hooks and explicit abort path that reverts host config and invalidates the profile key.
notes: We intentionally separate FP16 and INT8 candidate lanes: FP16 run is the baseline quick path; INT8 runs apply additional clipping and per-channel calibration.
FP8 experiments are shelved under ENG-21456-FP8-experiments (internal tag) for potential follow-up if INT8 achieves target cost savings but fails quality metrics.
Quant profiles must be semantically versioned and include a checksum so clients can detect mismatched profiles between control plane and runtime cache.
Prefer using cosine topk (k=10) median as the primary signal rather than global mean to reduce noise from rare extremes. Track both.
Add instrumentation for tokenization-related variance: ensure embedding inputs are normalized identically between FP32 baseline and quantized runtime.
